items.briefing:
Privacy advocates are calling for a ban on AI-powered smart glasses in Australia, citing serious concerns about covert filming and unauthorised recording of people in public and private spaces. The warning highlights how everyday consumer technology can pose real privacy risks, particularly in workplaces, training facilities, and public areas. Separately, South Australia has launched a Royal Commission into artificial intelligence, signalling growing government scrutiny of how AI is used across industries — including education and training.

**Practical tip:** If you notice someone wearing smart glasses or wearable tech in your workplace, check with your manager about your organisation's recording and privacy policy.

featured.title: South Australia launches Royal Commission into artificial intelligence
featured.quote: South Australia's Royal Commission into AI signals government-level scrutiny of artificial intelligence risks.
